literal: Those who cherish their own well-being will not embrace, proud of their beauty, those who display cheap pleasure, the shoulders.
translation: Those who cherish their own virtue and well-being will not embrace the shoulders of women who, proud of their physical charm, display and sell their cheap, worthless pleasures.
modern: தங்கள் நன்மையை விரும்புபவர்கள், அழகுச் செருக்குடன் தங்களின் மலிவான இன்பத்தை விற்கும் பொதுமகளிரின் தோள்களைத் தீண்டமாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet warns self-respecting individuals against associating with prostitutes. The author contrasts two groups: those who cherish their own true well-being ('தந்நலம் பாரிப்பார்') and those who merely trade in cheap, superficial pleasure ('புன்னலம் பாரிப்பார்'). The word 'தகைசெருக்கி' highlights how these women are proud of their outward beauty, which they use to lure others. By choosing not to touch their shoulders ('தோயார் தோள்'), wise people protect their character and dignity from being ruined by temporary, commercialized lust.
